analysis: This batch contains only test changes; no production source is included. NemotronSuperLocalImageBindingTests.swift (head 16-26) replaces the fixed 8 MiB+1 invalidInput expectation with NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes. It expects maximum+1 to fail with a new Failure.bodyTooLarge and the quote formula body*32 + template*4 + 16 MiB. The new NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests.swift exercises ingress of a body larger than 8 MiB, video inspection, frame decode and fixture serving. At line 112 it asserts that ingress plus plan totalBytes stays within Policy.videoMediaChargeBytes. Its fixtures are hash-pinned test resources (lines 52-56). NemotronSuperVideoBindingTests.swift line 168 raises the expected maximum video charge from 3,751,221,756 to 4,875,295,228 bytes. Lines 231-241 add a mapping from bodyTooLarge to media_too_large and leave invalidInput as invalid_media, both with status 400. The test comment says the coordinator returns 413. These changes imply production edits outside this batch: a larger encoded-body cap, a larger per-request media memory reservation (about 4.9 GB; TB-007/T-029 availability), and a new error code. Integration should verify the following. (1) maximumEncodedBodyBytes and the 32x ingress multiplier remain bounded before parsing and are charged against GlobalKVCacheBudget before decode. This affects provider DoS from adversarial consumers (ADV-002) through TB-002. (2) The raised video charge is reserved and refunded on every error and cancel path; the tests check that outstandingReservedBytes returns to baseline. (3) The new media_too_large failure is produced through sanitizedInferenceFailure and leaks no request content (T-008/A-001). (4) The coordinator maps it consistently. Tests cannot establish the production behavior, so no finding is raised. No changes touch attestation, keys, cache or authorization.
